step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify actors and external data sources: 'Users' (internal traders represented as UserCompanyDeveloper) triggers requests incorporating 'External Data' (ThirdParty).
2. Identify AWS services drawn on the whiteboard:
   - Application Load Balancer -> ALB
   - Pricing Engine, Pricing Workers (CPU), Pricing Workers (GPU) inside ECS -> ECS
   - Task Queues, Processing Queues, Pub/Sub, Payload inside ElastiCache for Redis -> ElastiCache
3. Tracing connections (arrows drawn in yellow):
   - Users -> External Data -> Application Load Balancer -> Pricing Engine
   - Pricing Engine -> Task Queues and Pricing Engine -> Payload
   - Task Queues -> Processing Queues
   - Task Queues -> Pricing Workers (CPU) and Pricing Workers (GPU)
   - Pricing Workers (CPU) and Pricing Workers (GPU) -> Payload

edges.notes: User triggers request taking in external market data
ALB routes request to Pricing Engine
Pricing Engine stores request payload in Redis
Pricing Engine puts job ID into Task Queue
Workers pop job from Task Queue into Processing Queue
CPU Workers pick up CPU jobs from Task Queue
GPU Workers pick up GPU jobs from Task Queue
CPU Workers retrieve payload and save results back to Redis
GPU Workers retrieve payload and save results back to Redis
